title: Give Home Assistant a home: Raspberry Pi
summary: Use one dedicated computer, protect its storage, and open Home Assistant on your network.
outcomes: Explain what the host computer does
Identify the Pi, power supply, storage and network
Record a verified first boot and a recoverable starting point

slides.title: One computer keeps the desk open
body: Host = the computer that runs Home Assistant
Choose Raspberry Pi OR the PC route
slides.narration: Think of Home Assistant as the front desk for your equipment. It needs a computer that stays on to receive readings and pass messages. That computer is the host. This route uses a Raspberry Pi. C2b uses a dedicated PC instead; choose one. If you already have a suitable working Home Assistant host, check its version and recovery plan and continue to C3. Keep watering equipment out of service during setup.

visual.title: One computer keeps the desk open
visual.alt: Choose one supported always-on computer: Raspberry Pi OR a dedicated x86-64 host.

slides.title: Lay out the parts first
body: Check the exact Pi model and its power supply
Use the official guide and wired network
slides.narration: A Pi is a small computer board, not a complete irrigation controller. You still need suitable power, storage, an enclosure, cooling and a network connection. The official guide lists Pi 4 or 5 with at least two gigabytes of memory and a card of at least thirty-two gigabytes. Check the current guide before buying. A plug that fits does not prove a charger supplies enough power. Use Ethernet for this installation.

visual.title: Lay out the parts first

slides.title: Example: choose the spare card
body: 64 GB spare card: checked and backed up
1 TB photo drive: leave it alone
slides.narration: Imagine your laptop shows a spare sixty-four gigabyte card and a one-terabyte photo drive. You want Home Assistant on the card. Writing the installation image replaces the selected storage contents. Identify the card by its device information and capacity, preserve needed files elsewhere, and leave the photo drive unselected. In Raspberry Pi Imager, choose Home Assistant OS for the exact Pi model and select the checked card.

visual.title: Example: choose the spare card

steps: Identify the spare 64 GB card.
Check its needed files have a separate copy.
Match the Home Assistant OS image to the exact Pi.
workedExample.answer: Only the identified, backed-up card is ready for writing.

slides.title: Your turn: the last check before Write
body: Name the device that will be erased
Check the model, image and separate backup
slides.narration: Before pressing Write, finish this sentence: I am replacing the contents of this identified card, and the files I need are copied here. Add the Pi model and matching image. If any answer is uncertain, resolve it before writing. Follow the official guide through writing and verification. Eject the finished card, insert it into the unpowered Pi, connect Ethernet on the same network as your computer, then connect the proper power supply.

visual.title: Your turn: the last check before Write

slides.title: Open the page on your own network
body: Use the local address in the official guide
Confirm this is the intended Pi
slides.narration: Start with the local Home Assistant address given in the official guide. If needed, use the Pi address found on your own network, with port eight-one-two-three where required. Confirm the page belongs to this Pi rather than an older Home Assistant host. A page opening tells you the computer is reachable. Probes and water controls still need their own checks. Continue to onboarding; do not test a pump just because the page loads.

visual.title: Open the page on your own network

slides.title: Keep a way back
body: Record model, storage, version and address
Continue to accounts and backups in C3
slides.narration: Now try a different case: a card holds old research files with no separate copy. What must happen before writing? Preserve the needed files and identify the destination again. For your completed installation, record the model, storage, installed version and local address. If boot fails, check power, network and official troubleshooting before another write. C3 adds accounts and backups. This record should let another responsible person understand how the host was prepared.

visual.title: Keep a way back

hints: Name the actual room, equipment and evidence you need.
Keep the example separate from a real installation.

title: Give Home Assistant a home: dedicated PC
summary: Use a supported dedicated PC instead of a Pi, identify its disk before erasing it, and check first boot.
outcomes: Explain why this PC must be suitable and dedicated
Distinguish the temporary USB system from the destination disk
Record a protected installation and verified first boot

slides.title: Another home for the same front desk
body: Choose the PC route OR Raspberry Pi
Use one suitable dedicated host
slides.narration: Home Assistant needs one computer that stays on, like a front desk that keeps receiving messages. This lesson uses a dedicated Intel or AMD PC. It reaches the same starting point as the Pi route; you do not need both. A small NUC-shaped computer may suit the job, but its shape or brand does not establish compatibility. Keep an existing suitable Home Assistant installation after checking it rather than erasing it for the lesson.

visual.title: Another home for the same front desk
visual.alt: Pi and x86-64 are alternative host routes; only one host is needed.

slides.title: Check the computer before changing it
body: 64-bit processor and UEFI boot
Protect files and record firmware settings
slides.narration: Use the official generic x86-64 guide to check the exact machine. It needs a sixty-four-bit processor, UEFI startup and supported storage. UEFI is the computer’s startup system. The guide requires storage that supports five-hundred-and-twelve-byte logical sectors; native four-kilobyte-only boot storage is unsupported. Disable Secure Boot as the official guide instructs. Writing Home Assistant OS replaces the selected disk’s operating system and files. Make a separate usable backup and record firmware settings first.

visual.title: Check the computer before changing it

slides.title: Example: the USB and disk have different jobs
body: USB: temporarily runs Ubuntu
Internal disk: receives Home Assistant OS
slides.narration: Picture a workbench with a temporary toolbox and a permanent cabinet. In the recommended installation method, a live Ubuntu USB is the toolbox: it starts a temporary operating system. The internal disk is the cabinet that receives Home Assistant OS. Boot the USB using Try Ubuntu, identify both devices by their information and capacity, and check the internal disk backup. Follow the official disk-image restore steps. Never copy another computer’s disk name.

visual.title: Example: the USB and disk have different jobs

workedExample.prompt: Which disk receives Home Assistant OS?
steps: Boot the temporary Ubuntu USB.
Identify the intended destination disk and its separate backup.
Check the target again at the destructive confirmation.
workedExample.answer: The verified destination disk; its existing contents will be replaced.

slides.title: Your turn: identify both devices
body: Live USB: ___. Destination disk: ___.
Read the destructive confirmation carefully
slides.narration: Fill in the live USB identity, intended destination disk, separate backup location and firmware changes. Before confirming the image write, say which disk will lose its contents. If Ubuntu is running from that destination disk, correct the boot choice rather than working around a busy-disk warning. After the official write and shutdown steps finish, remove the temporary USB as directed. The next start should use the Home Assistant disk.

visual.title: Your turn: identify both devices

slides.title: A capable office PC may still be unavailable
body: Current work files are not backed up
Its owner has not agreed to dedicate it
slides.narration: Now make the decision for a different machine. An office PC meets the processor requirements, but it still holds current work and nobody has agreed to dedicate it. Do not continue with the erase. Resolve permission, backups and its future job, or use another supported host. You can still study accounts, readings and the isolated demo. That learning does not depend on changing the office computer or risking its files.

visual.title: A capable office PC may still be unavailable

slides.title: Check first boot and write down the result
body: Use suitable power, cooling and Ethernet
Verify the host, version and local address
slides.narration: With the machine on suitable power and a reliable wired network, follow the official first-start steps. Open Home Assistant and verify that this particular host answers. Record the version and address alongside the hardware and backup details. If it fails, compare actual firmware and storage with official troubleshooting before another write. A working page establishes access. Continue to C3 for accounts, time and recovery; keep irrigation out of service until its own commissioning checks pass.

visual.title: Check first boot and write down the result

title: Install the software and protect access
summary: Understand Home Assistant labels, install both Crop Steering parts, and keep a recovery copy.
outcomes: Explain host, entity, integration and Controller in ordinary words
Install the matching integration and Controller using the documented HAOS steps
Verify the intended room, fresh Controller report, account access and separate backup

slides.title: The front desk gives each item an address
body: Entity = one named reading or control
A useful name still needs a physical label
slides.narration: Home Assistant gives each reading or control an address, called an entity ID. Think of sensor dot practice underscore moisture as a labelled letterbox: it tells software where to look. One probe can provide moisture, temperature and battery entities. The label alone cannot prove the probe’s location. During onboarding, set your local timezone, protect individual accounts and record recovery access without publishing passwords.

visual.title: The front desk gives each item an address

slides.title: Two Crop Steering parts do different jobs
body: Integration: settings, labels and workspace
Controller: decides when to water
slides.narration: Think of the integration as the interpreter and filing desk. It holds room settings and supplies the Crop Steering workspace inside Home Assistant. The Controller reads those settings and measurements and makes the watering decisions. You need both at matching versions. HACS is the community download library used to obtain the integration; downloading from it does not install the Controller. Before changes, keep watering disabled, confirm equipment state and preserve a backup outside the host.

visual.title: Two Crop Steering parts do different jobs

slides.title: Example: install the integration and room
body: HACS download, then restart Home Assistant
Start the Crop Steering configuration flow
slides.narration: If HACS is absent, install it through the guide first. Then open this project using its HACS link. Download the integration and restart Home Assistant. Then use the guide’s Crop Steering configuration link. Choose manual setup, name the room and enter its initial zone count. For example, name your paper room Practice Room with one zone. This creates its software record; it does not pair a probe or identify a valve. Use real names only after verification.

visual.title: Example: install the integration and room

workedExample.prompt: What has creating Practice Room established?
steps: Download the integration and restart Home Assistant.
Run its configuration flow and name the room.
Install and check the separate matching Controller next.
workedExample.answer: A named software room exists; physical mapping and delivery remain to be proved.

slides.title: Add and start the separate Controller
body: Add the project app repository
Install Controller; review options; start with watering OFF
slides.narration: Next use the guide to add the project to the app store’s list of sources, called app repositories. Install Crop Steering Controller from the Home Assistant app store at the same version as the integration. Review its options with affected watering controls OFF, then start the app. Check Start on boot and the documented Watchdog setting so it can restart after a failure. The HAOS Supervisor supplies its internal access token. Do not paste a secret into a repository file. Open Crop Steering in the Home Assistant sidebar.

visual.title: Add and start the separate Controller

slides.title: Your turn: a page opens but no report arrives
body: Workspace visible does not prove Controller running
Check the installed pair and report age
slides.narration: A fictional installation has a working workspace but no recent Controller report. Check that the separate Controller is installed, running and compatible before enabling anything. Its regular status message is called a heartbeat. A fresh heartbeat shows recent communication, not correct mapping or water delivery. Record both versions, the intended room and report age. If an older Controller already owns that room, resolve the documented upgrade or migration before starting another.

visual.title: Your turn: a page opens but no report arrives

slides.title: Keep a recovery copy you can actually use
body: Settings → System → Backups
Separate backup plus emergency kit where needed
slides.narration: In Home Assistant Settings, System, Backups, arrange a backup and keep a usable copy away from this host. Keep required decryption information, including the emergency kit for encrypted backups, securely available. A screenshot saying complete cannot restore a failed disk. Practise recovery on paper or isolated hardware, never by overwriting production for the lesson. Check local time against a clock. Room lighting hours are configured separately. Continue to C4 with watering still OFF.

visual.title: Keep a recovery copy you can actually use

practice.prompt: Prepare a software record with both installed versions, intended room, current Controller report, account-recovery method and separate usable backup.
hints: HACS download, room configuration and Controller app installation are separate steps.
A separate backup needs any required decryption information.

title: Tell the software which zone is which
summary: Map verified sensor and valve addresses, enter real sizing, and check that the Controller accepts the saved setup.
outcomes: Map one named zone to its physical equipment
Distinguish moisture, feed EC and identified root-zone EC measurements
Verify per-plant sizing, room time and Controller acceptance without enabling watering

slides.title: A contact name needs the right number
body: Mapping = linking the zone to its real addresses
Pair and verify devices in Home Assistant first
slides.narration: A phone contact can have a convincing name and still dial the wrong number. A zone mapping works the same way: its name must point to the right Home Assistant entities. First add each compatible device through its supported Home Assistant route. Check the exact entity ID against physical equipment labels. In Crop Steering, select the actual room and open Equipment, Setup. Keep affected Watering controls OFF and the installation’s required physical isolation in place.

visual.title: A contact name needs the right number
visual.alt: Actual isolated demo screen. Read the displayed room and current sample values; separate paper examples use fictional values.

slides.title: Match the real plumbing and measurements
body: Zone valves only OR a pump then zone valves
Check quantity, units, location and timestamp
slides.narration: Choose Zone valves only if that matches the supply, or A pump, then zone valves when a pump is required. Map a pump only if it actually exists. Each zone needs its intended valve. For moisture, check suitable VWC units, placement and the last update. For EC, identify feed, bulk substrate or pore-water measurement. These describe different places or methods. Leave unavailable optional data explicitly unavailable instead of borrowing an unrelated number.

visual.title: Match the real plumbing and measurements
visual.alt: Actual isolated demo screen. Read the displayed room and current sample values; separate paper examples use fictional values.

slides.title: Example: twelve plants, not one giant pot
body: 12 plants; 3 L substrate per plant
2 drippers per plant; measured 3 L/h each
slides.narration: Imagine twelve plants, each in three litres of substrate. Each plant has two drippers measured at three litres per hour each. Enter twelve plants, three litres per plant, two drippers per plant and three litres per hour per dripper. The total estimated delivery is twelve times two times three: seventy-two litres per hour. Thirty-six litres is the total substrate, not the per-plant entry. Delivery estimates describe water supplied, not water taken up by plants.

visual.title: Example: twelve plants, not one giant pot

workedExample.prompt: Estimate delivery for 12 plants with 2 drippers each at measured 3 L/h.
steps: 12 × 2 = 24 drippers.
24 × 3 = 72 L/h estimated zone delivery.
Keep substrate at 3 L per plant, not the 36 L total.
workedExample.answer: 72 L/h zone delivery; this does not measure plant uptake.

slides.title: Check the clock and the receipt
body: Timezone and room lighting hours are separate
Review configuration, save, then wait for acceptance
slides.narration: Record the local timezone, the room’s configured lights-on and lights-off hours, and the actual lighting system that owns the lights. Observe that they agree; the irrigation clock does not operate the lights. Review configuration with affected equipment confirmed OFF, then Save configuration. Saving is like sending a letter. Mapping acknowledged is the separate receipt from the Controller. Wait for acceptance of this revision. A fresh heartbeat alone does not supply it.

visual.title: Check the clock and the receipt

slides.title: Your turn: three faults in one record
body: Wrong-room moisture; blank lighting hours
Saved setup with no acknowledgement
slides.narration: Review eight plants, four litres per plant, one dripper each, measured at two point five litres per hour. Calculate the twenty litres per hour zone delivery. Now find the faults: the moisture entity belongs to the next room, lighting hours are blank, and the revision is saved but unacknowledged. All need correction before enabling. Correct arithmetic cannot repair a wrong probe address. Practise this record review in the isolated demo without connecting equipment.

visual.title: Your turn: three faults in one record

slides.title: Read the accepted setup back
body: Check Overview and Equipment → Probes
Record unresolved items; keep watering OFF
slides.narration: After acknowledgement, inspect the intended room in Overview and Equipment, Probes. Compare exact readings, units and age with the setup sheet. Verify sizing, measured-flow evidence, light timing and each output’s owner. Resolve an unreadable state instead of treating it as OFF. These checks show the intended software setup reached the Controller. C5 checks physical protections, and C6 proves delivery and stopping. Keep automatic operation disabled until those checks pass with the responsible local people.

visual.title: Read the accepted setup back
visual.alt: Actual isolated demo screen. Read the displayed room and current sample values; separate paper examples use fictional values.

hints: The correct per-plant substrate entry remains 4 L.

title: Make the physical equipment safe to test
summary: Check the documented sensor connection, proper equipment ratings, shutdown and one owner for every output.
outcomes: Trace a reading from the actual probe through its supported interface
Explain why software OFF differs from physical isolation
Record the approved protection, shutdown and sole owner before wet testing

slides.title: A stop message is not a disconnected machine
body: Software OFF stops Controller requests
Physical isolation protects work on the equipment
slides.narration: Think of software OFF as a message telling a driver to stop. Physical isolation is the installation’s actual way to remove the hazard. They do different jobs. Crop Steering Watering OFF blocks its shots, but another timer or manual switch may still operate equipment, and electrical power may remain present. Before physical work, agree the installer-approved electrical and water shutdown, who controls it and how everybody knows the equipment’s state.

visual.title: A stop message is not a disconnected machine

slides.title: Use the probe’s documented connection
body: Exact model, signal, power and compatible interface
Never infer wire function from colour
slides.narration: A matching plug is like a matching envelope: its contents may still be wrong. Check the exact probe, supply voltage, signal protocol, compatible interface and supported firmware. Some probes need a bridge before Home Assistant can read them. Prefer a documented assembled route for a first installation. Follow the maker’s placement and calibration instructions. Do not connect an unknown probe signal directly to a computer pin or copy wire colours from a different assembly.

visual.title: Use the probe’s documented connection

slides.title: Example: a number can be fresh and irrelevant
body: 22 °C tank temperature is not zone moisture
Probe contact and measurement method still matter
slides.narration: A fictional entity reports twenty-two with a recent timestamp. Its friendly name mentions the room, but its units are degrees Celsius and it measures the tank. It cannot stand in for moisture in that room’s substrate. Check quantity, units, real location, contact and age together. Apply the same care to EC: a bulk-conductivity reading does not become pore-water EC just because the field expects it. Verify any conversion and the range where it applies.

visual.title: Example: a number can be fresh and irrelevant
visual.alt: Actual isolated demo screen. Read the displayed room and current sample values; separate paper examples use fictional values.

workedExample.prompt: Can a fresh 22 °C tank reading fill zone moisture?
steps: Read the exact quantity and units.
Check the physical location.
Select the actual suitable moisture entity instead.
workedExample.answer: No; tank temperature is not substrate moisture.

slides.title: Check what starts and stops the pump
body: Installer checks starting load and protection
Agree bounded test and physical shutdown
slides.narration: A control device’s headline rating may describe a simple heater load, while a pump draws a different starting load. Have the competent installer check the real motor, control input, electrical ratings and required protection. This course supplies no mains-wiring instructions. Also agree dry-run, spill, backflow and unwanted-siphon arrangements appropriate to the design. Before any test, name what may energise, where water can discharge, what remains isolated and how the test will end.

visual.title: Check what starts and stops the pump

slides.title: Your turn: two controllers know the same valve
body: Old timer still active; Crop Steering OFF
One owner must be established before testing
slides.narration: Now consider a valve that an old timer can still open. You have also mapped it into Crop Steering, whose Watering switch is OFF. The timer remains another route to water, so the valve is not isolated. Record both routes and resolve ownership before commissioning. Never leave two independent controllers able to drive the same output. Keep read-only observation separate from commands. The local operator must still have an agreed way to maintain necessary crop care.

visual.title: Your turn: two controllers know the same valve
visual.alt: The old timer and new Controller must not both own an output.

slides.title: Close the physical checks before the wet test
body: Verify readings and safe output identity
Carry the checked setup sheet into C6
slides.narration: Trace each probe to its verified Home Assistant reading, then trace each control address back to the physical valve or pump. A competent installer can use an approved low-risk identity check where appropriate. Do not use a live crop as the first wiring indicator. Record equipment ratings, protections, sole ownership and shutdown. Unresolved hardware questions keep this stage incomplete. Continue to C6 only with an approved catch-test method and safe collection ready; no attractive dashboard can replace these checks.

visual.title: Close the physical checks before the wet test

hints: Name the actual room, equipment and evidence you need.

title: First water: catch it, measure it, stop it
summary: Use the approved equipment test first, then supervise a Controller cycle only after every readiness check passes.
outcomes: Distinguish the installer’s equipment test from an enabled Controller cycle
Calculate measured emitter flow and observe actual stopping
Keep Watering OFF until readiness passes, then record the supervised cycle and final state

slides.title: Two tests answer two questions
body: Equipment test: does the water path work?
Controller cycle: does the commissioned system work?
slides.narration: First test the tap and hose, then test the automatic instructions. These are separate commissioning stages. In stage one, Crop Steering Watering stays OFF while the installer uses an approved equipment-level procedure. OFF blocks Controller test shots too; do not try to bypass it. Agree a bounded duration, collection and physical shutdown. If no suitable equipment test procedure exists, obtain one before proceeding. Neither the demo nor a quiz can supply physical evidence.

visual.title: Two tests answer two questions

slides.title: Watch the whole water path
body: Collect safely and keep other zones dry
Follow the approved pump and valve sequence
slides.narration: With competent local supervision, remove only the isolation needed for that particular test. Use the manufacturer’s safe method and observe the intended outlet, other zones, relevant pressure and the required pump and valve sequence. Catch several emitters separately for the real measured runtime. Keep spills contained and shutdown available. Stop through the agreed method and observe actual water cease. A control icon changing colour does not establish that flow stopped or that unwanted siphon is absent.

visual.title: Watch the whole water path
visual.alt: Timed individual catches, observed stopping and a checked water path.

slides.title: Example: a cup becomes a flow measurement
body: 30 mL caught in 30 seconds
slides.narration: Suppose an emitter delivers thirty millilitres in thirty seconds. Divide by one thousand to get zero point zero three litres. Multiply by thirty-six hundred seconds per hour and divide by the thirty-second runtime. That is three point six litres per hour for this catch. Separate catches of thirty, thirty-three and thirty-seven millilitres reveal differences their total hides. Investigate against the actual design and measurement uncertainty. These example volumes are not real calibration evidence or a universal tolerance.

visual.title: Example: a cup becomes a flow measurement

workedExample.prompt: Convert 30 mL caught in 30 seconds into L/h.
steps: Record the actual emitter, runtime and test conditions.
workedExample.answer: 3.6 L/h for that emitter during this catch.

slides.title: Your turn: finish the catch record
body: 24 mL in 30 seconds = 2.88 L/h
Record cessation, siphon check and corrections
slides.narration: Try twenty-four millilitres in thirty seconds: zero point zero two four times thirty-six hundred divided by thirty gives two point eight eight litres per hour. Add the actual emitter, runtime and test conditions to the record. Investigate leaks or uneven delivery, correct them and repeat the relevant checks. Test independent protections using their approved methods. Never simulate faults by pulling random wires or power under load, or risk deadheading a pump.

visual.title: Your turn: finish the catch record

slides.title: A good catch is one part of readiness
body: Fresh probes and acknowledged mapping
Approved targets, light timing, protection and recovery
slides.narration: Now decide for a different record: the catch and stopping passed, but the latest mapping is saved without Controller acknowledgement. Keep Watering OFF. Before stage two, every required check must pass: correct room and outputs, fresh probes, accepted mapping, measured delivery, verified stopping, independent protections, lighting hours, timezone, approved local targets and recovery access. Update measured flow through the setup review and obtain acknowledgement. Do not enable just to repair incomplete software setup.

visual.title: A good catch is one part of readiness

slides.title: Supervise the first enabled cycle
body: Only after all required checks pass
Observe the actual event, stopping and final state
slides.narration: After readiness passes, the responsible operator deliberately enables the selected room’s Watering through the documented review and confirms its state. Enabling allows eligible shots, including safety watering. Use approved local settings, safe collection and competent supervision. Observe the intended outlet, other zones, actual stopping, event record and next action. If water continues unexpectedly, use the agreed physical shutdown and disable Watering. Record the result and explicitly agreed final state. Repeat the checks for each new output.

title: Move from Growlink one zone at a time
summary: Observe and record the existing system before a planned handover; keep one controller in charge of each output.
outcomes: Record the existing Growlink zone, measurements, timing and output ownership
Plan a controlled handover without assuming automatic import or compatible hardware
Verify one migrated zone with commissioning evidence and a usable rollback plan

slides.title: Moving house starts with a labelled inventory
body: Observe the existing system before changing it
Record one room and one physical zone
slides.narration: Moving from Growlink is like moving house: label what you have before disconnecting anything. Begin with observation and available records. Name one room, one physical zone, its probes, valves, pump and current controller. Record who can operate or recover it. A working Growlink setup is useful evidence about the existing system, not proof that the same hardware can connect to Home Assistant. Keep the existing operator responsible for crop care while planning.

visual.title: Moving house starts with a labelled inventory

slides.title: Keep the records in their original context
body: Save available exports or make a manual record
Keep units, timestamps and method labels
slides.narration: Use exports available in your actual Growlink account and product, or record visible settings and history manually. Do not assume an export feature, API or automatic importer exists. Preserve original files and dates. Note the timezone, lights-on and lights-off, substrate, plant and dripper counts, measured flow, targets and measurement methods. A number labelled EC needs its location and method. Similar field names in two systems do not guarantee the same meaning.

visual.title: Keep the records in their original context

slides.title: Example: one old zone, several new addresses
body: Old label: Room A, Zone 1
Match new addresses to the physical equipment
slides.narration: Imagine Growlink calls a valve Room A, Zone One. Your Home Assistant setup now has an entity with the same friendly name. That is a contact-book match, not physical proof. Trace the actual output and probe, confirm compatible interfaces, units and data age, and write exact new IDs beside the old record. Keep unknown items marked unknown. Reuse C4’s sizing and mapping checks; do not paste old targets into differently defined fields.

visual.title: Example: one old zone, several new addresses

workedExample.prompt: Does a matching valve name prove migration is ready?
steps: Preserve the original room and zone record.
Trace the physical output and verify the new entity ID.
Confirm compatible control and sole ownership before commissioning.
workedExample.answer: No; matching names alone establish neither physical identity nor exclusive control.

slides.title: Agree the handover and the way back
body: One controller owns each output at a time
Plan shutdown, crop cover and rollback
slides.narration: With the responsible operator and competent installer, agree when ownership changes, which controls are disabled, and how the crop receives necessary water during work. Establish one controller per physical output. The new system may observe where supported; it must not command the same valve alongside Growlink. Record physical isolation and the steps to restore the previous arrangement if checks fail. A rollback plan is a checked procedure, not permission to leave both schedules active.

visual.title: Agree the handover and the way back
visual.alt: Agree one output owner and a checked way back before the handover.

slides.title: Your turn: the name matches, the unit does not
body: Old EC method unknown; new field expects pore-water EC
Do not fill the gap by guessing
slides.narration: Review a different migration record. The old sensor is labelled EC, its method is unknown, and the new field expects pore-water EC. The valve name matches, but no physical identity check exists. Decide what to do. Park those mappings and investigate; a familiar display cannot close either gap. Keep the last verified arrangement under its agreed owner. Finish the checks from C3 to C5 before planning C6’s supervised catch and Controller stages.

visual.title: Your turn: the name matches, the unit does not

slides.title: Prove one zone before expanding
body: Repeat staged commissioning after handover
Record operation, final state and responsible owner
slides.narration: At the agreed handover, follow the approved shutdown and ownership procedure, then complete staged commissioning from C6. Check acknowledged mapping, fresh readings, real flow, stopping, approved targets and timing. Supervise the first enabled cycle and record its event and final state. If a check fails, leave the new output disabled and use the agreed recovery procedure. Expand only after this zone’s evidence is complete. Repeat for every output; one successful zone does not establish the rest.
